# OpenShell Dashboard Helm chart

<!-- Generated by helm-docs; edit README.md.gotmpl, then run `make helm-docs` -->

Deploys a stateless dashboard alongside an [OpenShell gateway](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/tree/main/deploy/helm/openshell). Only the oauth2-proxy sidecar is exposed on port 4180; the BFF listens on loopback port 8080. Gateway certificates, database, cluster RBAC, and certgen are external.

## Install: OpenShift Route + Keycloak

Install the upstream gateway in the **same namespace** as release `openshell` (or set `gateway.serviceName` / `gateway.url`). Match its `server.oidc.issuer`, `audience`, `rolesClaim`, `adminRole`, and optional `caConfigMapName` to chart `oidc.*`. For [Keycloak overlay](ci/values-keycloak.yaml), configure gateway `server.auth.allowUnauthenticatedUsers=false`, `server.oidc.audience=openshell-api`, `server.oidc.rolesClaim=resource_access.openshell-api.roles`, `server.oidc.adminRole=openshell-admin`, and `server.oidc.userRole=openshell-user`.

Create a confidential Keycloak client `openshell-dashboard`: register `https://<dashboard-host>/oauth2/callback` under **Valid redirect URIs** and `https://<dashboard-host>/oauth2/sign_in` under **Valid post logout redirect URIs**. Grant users `openshell-api:openshell-user` or `openshell-api:openshell-admin` client roles; standard users also need [workspace membership for token `sub`](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/agent-ops/blob/openshell-oidc-keycloak-docs/install/02-user-auth-keycloak.md#step-14-add-workspace-members). oauth2-proxy forwards its **access token** to the gateway: check its `aud` includes gateway `server.oidc.audience` (`openshell-cli` by default, `openshell-api` here) and its roles appear under `resource_access.openshell-api.roles`. `oidc.audience` documents this requirement; it cannot change tokens. Check the access token, not the ID token. Keycloak Audience Resolve can add API-client audience when roles are present; realm-role-only or authentication-only setups need an explicit audience mapper.

From repository root, create the Secret outside Helm. Choose an **existing** image tag with `--healthcheck` support; `v1.2.0` and earlier lack it, and source `appVersion=0.0.0` is unpublished. For published charts, use the version-matched image or a tested digest. Replace sample hosts and issuer:

```sh
NAMESPACE=openshell
KEYCLOAK_ISSUER=https://keycloak.apps.example.com/realms/openshell
KEYCLOAK_HOST=keycloak.apps.example.com
DASHBOARD_HOST=dashboard.apps.example.com
DASHBOARD_IMAGE_TAG=<image tag>

POST_LOGOUT_URL="https://${DASHBOARD_HOST}/oauth2/sign_in"
IDP_LOGOUT_URL="${KEYCLOAK_ISSUER}/protocol/openid-connect/logout?client_id=openshell-dashboard&post_logout_redirect_uri=$(jq -nr --arg url "$POST_LOGOUT_URL" '$url|@uri')"
LOGOUT_URL="/oauth2/sign_out?rd=$(jq -nr --arg url "$IDP_LOGOUT_URL" '$url|@uri')"

kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" create secret generic openshell-dashboard-oidc \
  --from-literal=client-secret='<client secret>' \
  --from-literal=cookie-secret="$(openssl rand -base64 32 | tr -d '\n')"

cd ./deploy/helm/openshell-dashboard
helm upgrade --install openshell-dashboard . \
  -n "$NAMESPACE" -f ./ci/values-openshift-scc.yaml \
  -f ./ci/values-route-edge.yaml \
  -f ./ci/values-keycloak.yaml \
  --set-string "oidc.issuer=$KEYCLOAK_ISSUER" \
  --set-string "openshiftRoute.host=$DASHBOARD_HOST" \
  --set-string "dashboard.image.tag=$DASHBOARD_IMAGE_TAG" \
  --set-string "dashboard.logoutURL=$LOGOUT_URL" \
  --set-string "authProxy.whitelistDomains[0]=$KEYCLOAK_HOST"
```

Follow Helm NOTES after installation. Logout returns to `/oauth2/sign_in` to avoid showing a stale dashboard; `authProxy.whitelistDomains` must include the IdP host. For another IdP, change both `LOGOUT_URL` and allowed redirect domain.

## Configuration

- **OIDC:** `oidc.provider=oidc` supports compatible issuers; use `oidc.allowedGroups` to restrict groups. For Keycloak realm/client role filtering use `oidc.provider=keycloak-oidc` and `oidc.allowedRoles` (any listed role). `oidc.scope` (default `openid email profile`) and `oidc.codeChallengeMethod` are optional. `oidc.clientIdSecretKey` overrides `oidc.clientId` using the existing Secret; set `oidc.caConfigMapName` only for a private issuer CA (also configure the gateway). Keep `authProxy.cookie.refresh` below access-token lifetime.
- **Gateway:** Default CA is `openshell-client-tls`/`ca.crt` from upstream certgen or cert-manager. `gateway.url` accepts `grpcs://`/`https://` for TLS or `grpc://`/`http://` for plaintext. For `server.disableTls=true`, use [TLS-disabled values](ci/values-tls-disabled.yaml) (no CA), but keep browser ingress HTTPS. Set `gateway.clientCertSecretName` only for mTLS without OIDC, with proxy users restricted by allowed groups/roles. `gateway.preflight.enabled=true` checks the Service on live installs; leave false for `helm template`.
- **Exposure:** [Route edge](ci/values-route-edge.yaml), [Route reencrypt](ci/values-route-reencrypt.yaml), [Gateway API](ci/values-gateway-api.yaml), [mTLS](ci/values-mtls-client-cert.yaml), [Keycloak](ci/values-keycloak.yaml), [TLS-disabled](ci/values-tls-disabled.yaml), and [OpenShift SCC](ci/values-openshift-scc.yaml) overlays are renderable examples; supply referenced Secrets/ConfigMaps, real hosts, and reencrypt destination CA. Set `oidc.redirectURL` if the public host is assigned dynamically. Edge Route terminates TLS before proxy: keep `authProxy.forceHTTPS=false` (secure cookies remain enabled). For reencrypt, supply `authProxy.tls.secretName` (Route-host certificate) and `openshiftRoute.destinationCACertificate` so the Route validates proxy TLS; set `authProxy.forceHTTPS=true` only with proxy TLS. HTTPRoute forwards HTTP to proxy and needs a TLS-terminating Gateway. Preserve Host and WebSocket upgrade headers; Route timeouts are 300s and 1h for terminal sessions.
- **Network:** NetworkPolicy permits ingress only to proxy port from `openshift-ingress` by default for Routes. For HTTPRoute, set `networkPolicy.ingressNamespace` or `networkPolicy.ingressFrom` for **data-plane proxy pods**, which may differ from Gateway namespace; hostNetwork/node-IP controllers need cluster-specific rules. Never expose BFF port 8080 directly: it bypasses auth.
- **Images/probes:** Dashboard defaults to `quay.io/gkrumbach07/openshell-dashboard:<appVersion>`; oauth2-proxy is pinned to `v7.15.5`. Dashboard probes exec `--healthcheck` against loopback; proxy HTTP probes use `/ping`. Override `probes.*.dashboardCommand` for another binary path. Chart/appVersion start at `0.0.0`; release CI stamps both and publishes `oci://ghcr.io/gkrumbach07/openshell-dashboard/helm-chart/openshell-dashboard`. Stable versions are immutable; pin chart version and image digest separately. Floating `0.0.0-dev` uses matching `sha-<commit>` image tag. For mirrors, override `global.image.registry` and component repository/digest.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |

| affinity | object | `{}` | Affinity. |
| authProxy.apiRoutes | list | `["^/api/"]` | API path patterns that return HTTP 401 instead of redirecting to the identity provider on an expired session. |
| authProxy.cookie.name | string | `"_oauth2_proxy"` | Session cookie name; use a distinct name when dashboards share a hostname. |
| authProxy.cookie.refresh | string | `"2m"` | Interval for refreshing the access token; set below the issuer's access-token lifetime. Empty disables refresh. |
